reference_job.query: CVE vulnerability exploitation events including in-the-wild attacks, public proof-of-concept exploit releases, and breaches attributed to named threat actors
reference_job.context: For each event, extract the primary CVE identifier (CVE-YYYY-NNNN), all CVE identifiers mentioned, whether a public proof-of-concept or working exploit code exists, the victim organization that was compromised (NOT the vendor whose product is vulnerable), the date the exploit or breach occurred (event date, distinct from publication date), and any named threat actors or APT groups attributed. Treat PoC release, active exploitation in the wild, and named-attacker breaches as events. Do not include routine patch advisories where no exploit has been observed.

validators.name: mentions_cve_identifier
validators.description: true if the article references at least one CVE identifier in CVE-YYYY-NNNN format

validators.name: describes_exploitation_or_poc
validators.description: true if the article describes active exploitation in the wild, a published proof-of-concept, working exploit code, or a breach attributed to a threat actor. false if the article only announces a patch with no exploit context.

enrichments.name: main_cve
enrichments.description: The single primary CVE identifier this article focuses on, in CVE-YYYY-NNNN format. If multiple CVEs are discussed, return the one the article centers on (typically the one in the headline or first mentioned). Return empty string if no CVE is found.

enrichments.name: severity
enrichments.description: CVSS severity classification if stated: 'Critical', 'High', 'Medium', 'Low', or empty string if not specified. Include the numeric CVSS score in parentheses if given, e.g., 'Critical (9.8)'.

enrichments.name: event_date
enrichments.description: The date the exploit, breach, or PoC release actually occurred. This is distinct from the article's publication date. Parse natural-language references like 'attacks observed since mid-March 2026', 'the breach occurred in February 2026 but was disclosed in April', or 'PoC was published on May 3, 2026'. If only a month is given, use the first day of that month. Return null if no event date can be determined.

enrichments.name: all_cve_codes
enrichments.description: Every CVE identifier mentioned in the article, as a comma-separated list in CVE-YYYY-NNNN format. Deduplicated. Example: 'CVE-2026-12345, CVE-2026-67890'.

enrichments.name: poc_available
enrichments.description: Whether a public proof-of-concept exploit, working exploit code, technical write-up enabling reproduction, or active in-the-wild exploitation exists. Return exactly one of: 'Yes', 'No', or 'Unknown'. Use 'No' if the article only describes the vulnerability without any exploit availability reference.

enrichments.name: threat_actors
enrichments.description: Named threat actors, APT groups, ransomware crews, or nation-state attribution mentioned in the article (e.g., 'Lazarus Group, Volt Typhoon', 'Cl0p', 'APT29'). Comma-separated. Return empty string if the article describes the activity as 'unknown attackers', 'state-sponsored hackers' without naming a group, or otherwise lacks named attribution.

enrichments.name: vendor_or_product
enrichments.description: The vendor and/or product whose vulnerability is exploited (e.g., 'Ivanti EPMM', 'Apache HTTP/2', 'Microsoft Exchange'). Distinct from the victim_organization field.

enrichments.name: victim_organization
enrichments.description: The organization that was compromised, breached, or actively targeted via this CVE. This is the VICTIM, not the vendor of the vulnerable product. For example, if attackers used a Microsoft Exchange flaw to breach Acme Corp, the victim is Acme Corp, not Microsoft. If the article describes the vulnerability generically with no named victim, leave the company fields empty.
